name: IRS2113MTRPBF
title: IRS2113M high and low side MOSFET and IGBT gate driver, 600 V, 4 mm x 4 mm MLPQ
summary: A two-channel gate driver for one high side and one low side N-channel MOSFET or IGBT, with a separate input for each output. HO lives on a floating channel, supplied by a bootstrap capacitor, whose return VS may sit as high as 600 V above COM; LO is referred to COM. Both outputs swing a 10 V to 20 V gate supply and deliver 2.5 A typical (2.0 A minimum) peak source and sink current. The logic side has its own 3.3 V to 20 V supply VDD and its own ground VSS, which may differ from COM by up to 5 V either way. Undervoltage lockout watches both gate supplies, a shutdown input SD forces both outputs low, and the two channel delays match within 20 ns. The package is a 16-position 4 mm x 4 mm MLPQ with two leads left out and an exposed pad.

pins.name: HIN
pins.function: Logic input that sets HO; HO is in phase with it. Schmitt trigger with a pull-down to VSS.

pins.name: SD
pins.function: Shutdown input: while high, HO and LO are both held low. Schmitt trigger with a pull-down to VSS.

pins.name: LIN
pins.function: Logic input that sets LO; LO is in phase with it. Schmitt trigger with a pull-down to VSS.

pins.name: VSS
pins.function: Ground of the logic side; the reference for the input thresholds and currents.

pins.name: LO
pins.function: Gate drive output for the low side switch, swinging from COM to VCC.

pins.name: COM
pins.function: Return of the low side driver; every absolute voltage rating is referred to it.

pins.name: VCC
pins.function: Supply of the low side driver, 10 V to 20 V above COM.

pins.name: VS
pins.function: Return of the floating high side supply: the source or emitter of the high side switch.

pins.name: VB
pins.function: Floating supply of the high side driver, 10 V to 20 V above VS.

pins.name: HO

circuits.title: Typical connection
circuits.description: A half bridge of two N-channel MOSFETs, each gate fed from its driver output through a series resistor. The upper MOSFET's drain sits on a bus of up to 600 V, decoupled to ground by C4; its source is the switch node, tied to VS and brought out as one load connection. The lower MOSFET's source and COM go to ground, and its drain is brought out as the other load connection. C2 across VB and VS is the bootstrap capacitor, recharged from VCC through D1. C3 decouples VCC to COM and C1 decouples VDD to VSS. HIN, SD and LIN come in as terminals beside VDD, VSS and VCC.

circuits.title: Floating supply voltage transient test circuit
circuits.description: The fixture for the 50 V/ns offset transient rating. One 15 V supply feeds VDD and VCC, decoupled to ground by 10 µF and 0.1 µF. HIN, SD, LIN, VSS and COM all go to ground, so both outputs are held low. A 10KF6 diode from the 15 V rail charges a 0.1 µF bootstrap capacitor across VB and VS. VS is fed from the HV supply (10 V to 600 V, 100 µF to ground) through a 200 µH inductor with a 10KF6 diode from VS up to HV; a second 10KF6 clamps VS to ground, and an IRF820 driven by a pulse through a buffer pulls VS down. VS and HO are the monitored outputs, slewed faster than 50 V/ns.

parts.note: VS to HV, across the inductor

circuits.title: Switching time test circuit
circuits.description: The fixture the dynamic characteristics are measured in. One 15 V supply feeds VDD and VCC, decoupled to ground by 10 µF and 0.1 µF, and VSS and COM go to ground. A separate 15 V supply sits between VB and VS, decoupled by 0.1 µF and 10 µF, and VS is set anywhere from 0 V to 600 V, decoupled to ground by 10 µF. HO carries a load capacitance CL to VS and LO one to ground; HIN, SD and LIN are driven from outside.

parts.note: HO load to VS; CL = 1000 pF for the dynamic characteristics
LO load to ground; CL = 1000 pF for the dynamic characteristics

operation.text: LO is powered from VCC and referred to COM. HO is powered from VB and referred to VS, a floating channel meant for a bootstrap supply, so it can drive an N-channel MOSFET or IGBT on the high side of a bridge up to 600 V. The floating channel stands negative transients on VS and is immune to dV/dt up to 50 V/ns.

HIN, LIN and SD are CMOS Schmitt-trigger inputs with pull-downs, accepting standard CMOS or LSTTL levels and logic as low as 3.3 V. They run from their own supply VDD (3.3 V to 20 V) and ground VSS, which may sit up to 5 V either side of COM. With VDD at 15 V the thresholds are 9.5 V minimum for a one and 6.0 V maximum for a zero; both scale with VDD (figures 12B and 13B).

Each output follows its input in phase. While SD is high both outputs are low. Shutdown acts on edges, cycle by cycle: an output that SD turned off stays off after SD goes low again, until its input next rises (figure 1). The two channels' delays match within 20 ns.
Each gate supply has its own lockout: VBS for the high side, VCC for the low side. Typical thresholds are 8.6 V rising and 8.2 V falling on VBS, 8.5 V rising and 8.2 V falling on VCC.

The output buffers are built for high pulse current with little cross-conduction inside the driver: 2.5 A typical, 2.0 A minimum source and sink into a short for pulses of 10 µs or less at 15 V bias. Into 1000 pF the outputs rise in 25 ns and fall in 17 ns typical.

Each logic input has a pull-down resistor to VSS, ESD diodes to VDD and VSS and a series resistor ahead of the input stage. HO and LO have ESD diodes to their own rails. 25 V clamp diodes sit across VB-VS, VCC-COM and VDD-VSS and between VCC and VSS, and a 600 V diode runs from COM to VB.

The most negative VS the high side withstands moves further below COM as VBS rises, from about -3 V at VBS = 10 V to about -8 V at 20 V (figure 36, typical). The largest positive VSS offset the logic withstands grows with VCC, from about 6.5 V at VCC = 10 V to about 14 V at 20 V (figure 37, typical).

Figures 28 to 35 give junction temperature against switching frequency for lines labelled 10 V, 140 V and 320 V, with VCC = 15 V, driving an IRFBC20 (RGATE 33 Ω), IRFBC30 (22 Ω), IRFBC40 (15 Ω) or IRFPE50 (10 Ω): figures 28 to 31 for the IRS2110/IRS2113, 32 to 35 for the IRS2110S/IRS2113S. Temperature stays near 25 °C up to about 1E+4 on the kHz axis and climbs steeply above 1E+5, faster on the higher-voltage lines.
Pad 17 is grounded internally; tying it to COM improves electrical performance.
